full_judgment:
10. Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs while giving its opinion accorded undue benefit to writ petitioners of Writ Petition No. 3968 of 2002 appointed after 1985 who could not succeed in the writ petition by making out a case of discrimination and also excluded and dropped the most important part of the observation of judgment of High Court Division at the time of passing the opinion. After encadrement of 230 Thana family planning officers in 1985, left out 234 officers were waiting in the Zone of encadrement by promotion against the one third quota prescribed in BCS (Health and Family Planning; Family Planning) Recruitment Rules, 1986. Out of them 65 officers were encadred by promotion in cadre post in 1994, 14 officers in 1996, 9 officers in 1997, 55 officers in 1998, 3 officers in 1999, and 3 officers in 2001 totaling 149. Out of remaining 85 (234-149 = 85) officers, only 34 were petitioners in Writ Petition No. 3968 of 2002 who had been able to make out a case of discrimination and succeeded in the writ petition to get seniority with effect from 11-9-1995. Rest 160 officers having been appointed-after 1985 and onwards could not make out the case of discrimination as they were not in service in 1985 while such discrimination had taken place. Thus, if the government decides to encadre the officers appointed after 1985 their seniority shall have to be fixed under the provision of the BCS Seniority Rules, 1983 as observed by High Court Division. 

 11. Contemnor Nos. 1, 3, 4 & 5 entered appearance by filing separate Vokalatnama. Out of them, only contemnor No.3 contested the Rule by filing, affidavit-in-opposition denying all the material allegations as stated in the contempt peti- tion stating inter alia, is that, contemnor No. 3 being the government official holds the judiciary) with great esteem. He never intentionally or knowing fully disobeyed any order or direction passed by this Court and never intended to do so and he has the highest respect and honour towards the dignity and prestige of the Court and as responsible and conscious citizen contemnor No. 3 deems it obligatory on his part to place the correct position of the unfortunate situation in which he finds himself not in a spirit of contest but in a spirit of serving the cause of the truth. Petitioners have misunderstood and misconstrued the decision, findings and observations of High Court Division, as the whole case of writ petitioners of Writ Petition No. 3968 of 2002 was encadrement of 234 family planning officers in the cadre strength and their seniority with effect from 11-9- 1995. Present contempt-petitioners also filed another petition being No. 2650 of 2003 and the Rule issued in that writ petition was discharged by High Court Division by judgment and order dated 8-12-2009 (Annexure- "1"). Contempt petitioners also filed a case before the Administrative Tribunal being AT Case No. 84 of 2003 in respect of self same matter but the same was dismissed for default. Therefore, the instant contempt-petition filed with frivolous and vague allegations on the basis of misinterpretation of the judgment is liable to be dismissed. 

 13. The allegation of manipulation of the appointment/posting/ current charge/additional current charge were neither subject matter of Writ Petition No. 3968 of 2002 nor any Rule was issued or nothing was decided by High Court Division in that regard by the judgment passed in the writ petition. Contempt petitioners could not make out a single case of defiance, non-compliance or disobedience of judgment and order of High Court Division passed in Writ Petition No. 3968 of 2002. Government has taken necessary steps to do the needful to implement the judgment of the High Court Division dated 8-12-2009 and the matter is under process. 

 19. Contempt-petitioners also filed two affidavits-in-reply against the affidavit-in-opposition filed by contemnor No.3 and added opposite party Nos. 6 and 7, stating in short, is that subject matter of Writ Petition No. 2650 of2003 and AT. Case No. 84 of 2003 were totally different. Said two cases were filed challenging an SRO by which 64 posts of Assistant Director and 50 posts of Assistant Director (CC) of Department of Family Planning had been treated as non-cadre post because the understanding of cadre officers was that the said posts were cadre posts. But at the time of hearing when learned Advocates of respondents submitted that those post holders themselves claimed as non-cadre post holders than their Lordships were pleased to discharge the Rule with observations. Another set of cadre officers who filed the AT Case before the Administrative Tribunal did not press the case on similar ground. 

 20. It is true that government has power to increase/decrease cadre strength but it does not have any unguided and arbitrary power to give a favourable consideration to a particular group of people by encadring them in violation of BCS Recruitment Rules of 1981 and BCS Seniority Rules, 1983 which has been done in the instant case. After promulgation of BCS (Health & Family Planning: Family Planning) Recruitment Rules, 1986 service of the entire family planning department came under said Rules. It has been prescribed in the Rules that entry post of Thana family planning officer in the BCS (Family Planning) cadre would be filled up 2/3rd by promotion from family planning officers, who were in the pay scale of NNS Taka 625-1,315 (MNS Taka 1,350-2,750) having 3 years experience. On the day of promulgation of the Rules, 140 out of 464 family planning officers who were in the selection grade of NNS Taka 750-1470 (MNS Taka 1,650-3,020) were absorbed and 90 Thana family planning officers who were in the pay scale ofNNS Taka 625-1315 (MNS Taka 1,315-2,750) were promoted. Out of 234, all class-II officers who were in the pay scale ofNNS Taka 625-1,315 (MNS Taka 1,315-2,750) having 3 years experience were encadred against 1/3rd promotion quota till 1998. In 1998 when all posts were upgraded to class-l with effect from 11-9-1995 scope of encadrement by way of promotion against 1/3rdquota of class-II had been blocked and stopped. Opposite parties and other class-II officers had accepted their up-gradation to class-I non-cadre posts knowing fully well that their encadrement by way of promotion in BCS (Family Planning) cadre would be stopped for good. 

 29. To elaborate his argument, Mr Karim submits that if the petitioners are given seniority over added-opposite party Nos. 6 and 7 and other writ petitioners joined after 1985 at the time of their encadrement in DCS (Family Planning) cadre, then judgment of High Court Division shall be violated and such action shall be contemptuous inasmuch as added-opposite party Nos. 6 and 7 and writ petitioners joined after 1985 were upgraded to class-1 gazetted officers in the corresponding pay scale of Taka 750-1,470 before con- tempt petitioners were appointed as first class gazetted officers in the corresponding pay scale of Taka 750-1,470 and petitioners as well as added opposite party No. 6 and 7 including writ petitioners joined after 1985 are in the same post of family planning officer of same rank and pay scale and also discharging same responsibilities. As such under the facts and circumstance of the case, no offence of contempt of Court have been committed by the contemnors at the implementation process of the said judgment and order dated 8-12-2009 by including added-opposite party Nos. 6 and 7 and writ petitioners joined after 1985 in BCS (Family Planning) Cadre and giving them seniority over the petitioners with effect from 11- 9-1995 and thus the Rule should be discharged. 

 32. Let us decide the question of maintainability first. Admittedly contempt petitioners were added respondents in the writ petition and they were interested parties to the matter in dispute. Petitioners are directly recruited BCS cadre family planning officers and writ petitioners including opposite party Nos. 6 & 7 are non-cadre family planning officers in the same department. Now the sole dispute between said cadre and non-cadre officers is the question of seniority. The contention of contempt petitioners is that non-cadre family planning officers who were appointed after 1985 would get seniority from the date of their encadrement in the cadre as per Seniority Rules, 1983 as directed by this Division in judgment dated 8-12-2009; but the government violating the direction of this Division decided to give them seniority over cadre officers including petitioners with effect from 11-9-1995 and, as such, contempt petitioners have constrained to file this contempt petitioner under Article 108 of the Constitution to protect their right and to compel the government to implement the judgment as per directions and observations given therein as there is no other forum available to them to implement the judgment of this Division. In the case of Government of Bangladesh, represented by the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka vs Mrs Anwara Huq reported in 9 MLR (AD) 253 = 56 DLR (AD) 185 our apex Court held: 

 37. In the case of Md Abdul Halim vs Dr Md Tareque reported in 63 DLR 465 (where one of us was a party) after elaborate discussions relating to contempt matters held: 

 38. Now it is well established that the power of committal for contempt is given to the Superior Courts in order that they may swiftly and summarily perform one of their most important duties which is to protect themselves against willful disregard or disobedience of their authority. This summary power of punishing for contempt should be used sparingly and only in serious cases. To bring home an action within the mischief of contempt in the absence of any definition available in the Contempt of Court Act itself, it can be inferred that only the willful and deliberate disobedience of the Courts order can he considered to be the main ingredient to constitute a contempt of Court in a given situation. Proceedings for contempt of Court are of a quasi-criminal in nature and where there is any reasonable doubt, the person charged with contempt is entitled to benefit of doubt. 

 In this case we have found that the left out family planning officers who had requisite qualifications for being encadred were discriminated and they were entitled to be encadred along with those 230 encadred family planning officers." 

 "Now the question of seniority. The learned Advocates for the respondents 6-22 have advanced strong arguments in support of their contention that the writ-petitioners, if included in the cadre service, will get seniority from the date of their entry in the cadre service. Referring to rule 3(e) of BCS (Seniority) Rules, 1983 the learned advocates have argued that since there is no provision for lateral entry in the family planning cadre service the seniority of the petitioners, if are encadred, will have to be counted, from the date of their appointment to the lowest post in this cadre service i.e. the date of their encadredment as family planning officer. To strengthen this argument the learned Advocates have cited some instances also where seniority was given from the date of entry in the cadre service We very much appreciate these argument and contention of the learned advocates for the respondents 6- 22. We also do not differ with the decisions cited by the learned advocates. But we are unable to find that these decisions and instances cited by the learned advocates have any application in the present case-the facts and circumstances of which are totally different." 

 "However, taking into consideration the above views of the courts of this region and also the facts and circumstances of this case our considered opinion is that the writ-petitioners-who are entitled to be encadred-will get seniority in the cadre service from the date of their being entitled to be encadered i.e. from 11-9-1995." 

 49. Now let us see as to whether the contemnors committed contempt of Court considering the facts and circumstances of the instant case. We have carefully scrutinized Annexure Band D-to the contempt petition as well as Annexure IV, V, VI, VII and VITI to the supplementary affidavit filed by contemnor No.3. Annexure-B is the memo dated 22-2-2010 issued by Md Abdul Quayum, the then Director General of Family Planning Directorate, who gave proposal to contemnor No.3 the Secretary, Ministry of Health and Family Planning to increase cadre strength by including 34 non-cadre posts in the cadre schedule of BCS (Family Planning) Cadre to enable 34 writ petitioners (who were appointed before 1985) to encadre in the said cadre. Annexure-D is the memo dated 15-9-2010 issued by contemnor No.4, another Director General of Family Planning Directorate, who gave proposal to respondent No.3 to encadre all the writ petitioners of Writ Petition No. 3968, (appointed before and after 1985) in BCS (Family Planning) Cadre who were still in service. Annexure IV is the legal opinion of the Ministry of Law, Justice and parliamentary Affairs dated 26-12-2010, who gave opinion to implement the judgment without giving any opinion in respect of fixing seniority, Annexure- V is the approval letter of Ministry of Establishment dated 23-3-2011, who approved non-cadre 250 posts to be included in BCS (Family Planning) Cadre. Annexure-VI is approval letter of Finance Division of the Ministry of Finance dated 16-5-2011 who gave approval of said 250 posts to be included in the cadre strength, Annexure-VII is another approval of Finance Ministry dated 8-6-2011 who determined the pay scale of Taka 11,000-20.370 (scale No.9) of those 250 posts of Upazilla family planning officers and Annexure-VIII is the minutes of the meeting of the Secretaries Committee for Administrative Development of the Cabinet Division dated 4-12-2011 who gave Final recommendation to declare 250 non-cadre posts as BCS (Family Planning) Cadre posts by fixing the seniority of the newly encadred officers in the said posts with effect from 11-9-1995 in the following manner: 

 (6) Review of Seniority-The Government reserves the right to review any case of seniority as it deems fit."
